title: MigrationScan report
description: Output of `migrationscan`, schema 1.6. Additive and backward-compatible over 1.0: every field added since is optional, so a consumer written against an earlier minor keeps working. See docs/schema/README.md for consumer notes.

schemaVersion.description: Major.minor. An unknown major must be refused; a newer minor is additive and safe to read.

target.description: The TFM the root summary and projects describe, e.g. net10.0 or net10.0-windows.

redacted.description: Present and true when file paths were replaced with opaque ids. Absent means paths are real. Stated outright so an absent `file` is never ambiguous between 'redacted' and 'this finding has no file'.

scan.description: What produced the report. Deliberately carries no timestamp — identical input yields byte-identical output.

commit.description: Commit the scanned tree was checked out at, when it is a git working copy.

targets.description: Both portability stances from one scan (1.5+). Only summary and projects differ between them; findings, references, notAssessed and warnings are shared.

effort.description: Heuristic engineer-day range. Already applies per-rule bands and a sub-linear occurrence factor — build on it, do not re-derive from raw findings.

needsDecision.description: Blocking issues excluded from the day range: unbounded until an architectural decision is made.

totalFindings.description: Active findings only. On a Windows stance, satisfied lock-in findings are excluded.

windowsLockInSatisfied.description: Omitted on a cross-platform stance, where nothing is satisfied.

thirdPartyReferences.description: Distinct components, not declaration sites — fewer than the length of `references`.

path.description: Repo-relative project path. Kept even when redacted: it is the project's identity, and grouping by project is what makes a downstream proposal readable.

default.description: Marks the stance the document root describes. Absent on the other.

satisfiedPlatform.description: This stance satisfies findings whose `platform` equals this value. Absent on the cross-platform stance.

not.description: `file` and `fileId` are alternatives, never both: a redacted report replaces the field rather than redefining what `file` means.

file.description: Repo-relative path. Omitted when the finding has no file, and when the report is redacted.

fileId.description: Opaque, stable id standing in for a file path in a redacted report. Two findings in one file share an id.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity across runs and across redaction, used by --baseline. Excludes the line number so a finding survives edits that shift lines.

platform.description: Present only for Windows lock-in rules.

satisfiedByTarget.description: Present only when the document's target satisfies this lock-in finding.

reference.description: Inventory, not a finding: no severity, no effort, never trips --fail-on.

name.description: Identity, not location — kept even when redacted, because a component cannot be researched without it.

source.description: HintPath, project path, COM type-library GUID, or service URL. When redacted: a COM GUID is kept (identity), a service URL keeps only its scheme, anything else becomes an opaque id.
